The son will most likely lose. He is an intended third-party beneficiary, but his rights vest only when he learns of the contract and assents to it, relies on it, or sues. The landscaper and owner modified the payee before he knew anything, so the owner's payment to the landscaper discharged the obligation. The team note is wrong, because under the modern rule (Restatement (Second) §311) vesting does not occur at signing.

CONFIDENCE: 80
